title: Risk-Temporal Slicing and Lightweight A/B Protocol (working notes)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a lightweight A/B + canary protocol that uses temporal slicing (time-based micro-slices) to safely test LLM features with minimal cohort churn and clearer signal isolation. Goal is a fast, low-friction pattern product teams can use for iterative LLM feature launches and model parameter experiments while preserving observability and rollback simplicity.

Why temporal slices?
- Many existing slices (by user cohort, geography) add complexity to routing and billing.
- Temporal slices let us expose the new behavior to small windows of traffic, preserve the same user cohorts, and reduce cross-slice contamination for short-lived regressions.
- Temporal approach pairs well with LLM nondeterminism: we can collect contiguous windows of requests where upstream state is similar and run lightweight human-in-the-loop checks between windows.

Core concepts:
1) Micro-window (MW): 15–60 minute contiguous time window where 100% of incoming requests matching the experiment route are handled by variant B.
2) Pulse cadence: repeated MWs spaced by baseline windows (e.g., 30m on, 90m off) to collect multiple independent samples.
3) Lightweight AB: compare variant A (prod) vs B (candidate) aggregated across MWs. We avoid long sustained exposure for initial tests.
4) Strobing: a deterministic on/off schedule so routing changes are predictable and reversible without immediate customer-visible rollback.

Recommended quick-run recipe (starter template):
- Preflight (day -1): define hypothesis, primary metrics, abort conditions, P0 owners, and who will watch the first MW. Link a short ticket and a 1-pager.
- Traffic shaping: route split = 0% -> use pulse cadence for MWs; no persistent cohort assignment.
- MW schedule (example): 00:00–00:30 baseline (A), 00:30–01:00 MW1 (B), 01:00–02:30 baseline (A), 02:30–03:00 MW2 (B). Repeat until sample size target met or abort triggered.
- Observation: watch P95 latency, token cost per request, error counts, hallucination flag rate (from quality probes), user fallout metric where available, and discrete evaluation metrics from eval harness.
- Decision: after 3 MWs with consistent improvement or parity -> expand to longer canary; if any abort condition tripped -> immediate revert to A and incident postmortem.

Signal matrix (priority order):
1) Safety: runtime errors, request timeouts, increased 5xxs (+25% over baseline), signaled hallucination surge (custom probe) -> immediate abort.
2) Latency: 95th-percentile latency increase > 2x baseline or absolute > configured SLO -> abort or throttle candidate.
3) Cost: average tokens per completion jump > 15% -> require finance product approval before expansion.
4) Quality: degraded automated eval score (>3% drop relative) or increased user negative-feedback events -> pause.
5) Observability sanity: missing traces/logs for candidate -> treat as failed and revert.

Quick abort heuristics (for first MW):
- If any of the top-3 safety signals fire, send an immediate Slack page to #prod-rollouts and trigger a routing rule that swaps to A within 30s.
- If latency or token cost regressions appear but are marginal, reduce MW length by half and run 2 more pulses.

Statistical notes (very rough):
- We assume each MW approximates an independent sample. For binary success metrics (e.g., conversion) and low base rates, MWs should be sized to collect at least ~200 positive events across pulses; otherwise rely on qualitative checks.
- This protocol is intentionally not a replacement for rigorous long-running A/B tests for high-confidence product decisions. It's for early-signal safety and quality checks.

Operational runbook (starter):
- Owners: feature PM + experiment steward (engineer) + oncall SRE.
- Prep checklist: link to ticket, smoke test scripts, synthetic probe set, eval harness run, rollback route id, monitoring dashboard instance.
- During MW: experiment steward posts start timestamp and immediate impressions in doc. SRE watches infra metrics. PM monitors product metrics and user comms channel.
- Post-MW: quick debrief (5–10m) summarizing top signals. If ambiguous, run one more MW. After decisive pass, schedule gradual traffic expansion and longer canary (multi-day).

Implementation snippets / routing notes (pseudo):
- Route config: {route: "/api/generate", schedule: [{start: 2026-01-13T00:30:00Z, end: 2026-01-13T01:00:00Z, variant: B}, ...]}
- Fallback: all routes must include fallbackVariant: A and TTL for cache keys to avoid sticky state.
- Telemetry tags: experiment_id, mw_id, pulse_index, variant. Ensure these go into logs and traces.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to surface hallucination probes (synthetic vs production): need a standard small prompt set for each LLM surface. (Action: Lina to draft mini-eval of 20 prompts).
- Billing attribution for micro-windows: do we bill tokens to the same upstream cost center if variant differs? (Finance question).
- SDK changes: should we add a convenience parameter for pulse cadence in the SDK to reduce config friction? (Propose small RFC).
- Long-term: integrate temporal-slicing with cohort-slicing and assign hybrid experiments when cohort heterogeneity is suspected.

Notes to self / voice-of-doc:
- This is intentionally small and conservative. Use this when: fast experiment, model parameter tweak, reranker probational change, or new decoding heuristic. Do NOT use for major model architecture swaps.
- Keep the first 3 MWs supervised and keep pulses short. Our goal is to catch catastrophic regressions without exposing large cohorts.

Example quick log template (to paste into Slack or doc):
- experiment_id: PROD-TEMP-045
- variant: B (nucleus sampling 0.92)
- MW1 start: 2026-01-13T00:30Z
- steward: Arjun Patel
- immediate flags: latency +12% (P95), 5xxs normal, hallucination probes +0.5% (within noise)
- action: continue to MW2 as planned

Appendix: links and references
- See lightweight canary template (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/lightweight-canary-template
- Routing RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/446
- Slack channels: #prod-rollouts, #sre-oncall, #llm-quality

End notes: feedback welcome. This can be converted to a short checklist card in the console for quick one-click experiment creation (follow-on project).

-- Maya
